| f4 | defect | MINOR | npmVersionAtLeast fails OPEN on prereleases of the floor version. The regex `^\s*v?(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)(?:[-+].*)?\s*$` captures major/minor/patch and DISCARDS the prerelease identifier, so '11.10.0-rc.0' compares exactly equal to '11.10.0', the loop falls through to `return true`, and the guard reports the quarantine enforceable. Under semver, 11.10.0-rc.0 precedes 11.10.0 and may predate the min-release-age implementation. This is the one place the comparator deviates from semver ordering, and it deviates in the unsafe direction for a fail-closed control. | harness/scripts/release-age-policy.ts:16-27 | — | Narrow band (only prereleases of the floor release itself), which is why it is MINOR and not MAJOR — 11.9.9-rc is still correctly refused, and 12.0.0-rc is correctly allowed. Smallest fix: treat a captured prerelease suffix as strictly lower when major/minor/patch are all equal, i.e. if every numeric part matches and `current` has a prerelease while `required` does not, return false. This is the author's own self-named least-confident area, and it is the only defect I found in the comparator. | — | — | — | read of the regex and the equal-parts fallthrough at release-age-policy.ts:16-27 |
